reasoning_traces.think:
Structural balance arises from the principle that social networks tend toward stability through triadic closure, where relationships either reinforce or neutralize each other. This leads to a mathematical formulation involving signed graphs and parity constraints on triangles. In GSI, this translates into probabilistic models of market sentiment and agent alignment. Tie strength, derived from frequency and intensity of interaction, forms the basis of influence propagation and centrality metrics. It enables GSE to predict cascading effects in information diffusion. Homophily reflects the tendency of individuals to associate with similar others, which can be quantified as a normalized inner product of feature vectors. These primitives together define a layered framework for modeling complex systems with both static topology and dynamic behavior.
